correctness.rationale: For centered affine-regular hexagons H=conv{±u,±v,±(v−u)} with nonsingular u,v, area=3|det(u,v)|. Regular unit octagon has eight facets n_j·z≤1 over Q(√2), n_j=(±1,±(√2−1)) or swapped. Dihedral symmetry fixes u on first edge. The boundary conditions for v and v−u reduce via facet enumeration to three positive determinant edge chambers (and reflected negative partners), with quadratic D_i(s) and parameter intervals in frozen RESULT.md. Independently symbolically differentiated all three D_i and verified their endpoint maximum (3−√2)/2, unique interior minimum (2+3√2)/8 at s=1/2−√2/4, 1/2, 1/2+√2/4, with middle chamber spanning the full range. The area spectrum is 3 times determinant interval, divided by octagon area 2√2 for normalized interval. Independently enumerated 8^5 possible active facet assignments for general translated center c (using linear solves and linear-program feasibility): 3392 rank-deficient facet systems, 29 feasible polyhedra and no detected noncentral nondegenerate sampled vertex-pair solutions; this computational exploration does not by itself formally prove centrality or exhaustive positive-dimensional interior cases. Lassak 2003 explicitly treats the same center o of K and inscribed H in its extremal theorem, consistent with the centered reduction. Bundled verify.py has complete symbolic chamber enumeration but uses high-precision float comparisons for signs, so call it exact symbolic formulas with numerically classified signs, not fully certified sign arithmetic.
